newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians begin voting in key general election.
newsitem.headline: Albanians begin voting in key general election.

text.p: Albanians began voting in a make-or-break general election on Sunday under a state of emergency imposed to halt civil violence threatening to tear their Balkan country apart.

European nations and the United States, which have sent observers to monitor the poll, hope the election will restore political stability after more than 1,500 people were killed in months of disorder.
But the European envoy to Albania, Franz Vranitzky, has said the election is being held in unusual circumstances and will not be perfect.
Voters started trickling into the 4,525 polling stations across the mountainous country under a hot morning sun. Some two million Albanians are eligible to vote.

Polling stations will close at 6 p.m., three hours earlier than planned because of safety fears for voters and the some 500 international observers overseeing the country's third multi-party election since the fall of communism in 1990.
A 7,000-strong multinational protection force, sent into Albania in April to try to restore some calm, will escort and protect observers at polling stations and official counts.
The election pits the right-leaning Democratic Party of Sali Berisha, president since 1992, against the main opposition Socialists and 25 other political groups.
A total of 1,112 candidates are standing for the 155-member parliament in which 115 seats are allocated in first-past-the-post races and the rest on a proportional basis.
A runoff poll will be held on July 6 for the two top candidates in constituencies where no one wins 50 percent.
Sunday's first round is being combined with a referendum on whether to restore the monarchy, which ruled for 10 years before King Zog fled the country in April 1939.
First results should begin trickling into Central Electoral Commission headquarters in Tirana late on Sunday but overall unofficial results were not expected until Tuesday.
